items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: He had all them people and he could arrange and he used to arrange for the clarinet player, the fellow now, Benny Goodman.

ctx.x: No, I don't. Well, I tell you, in 1919 Fletcher Henderson came to Boston and he was the greatest band in the world there, because he could play waltzes, and that's the Massachusetts -- what's the name of the hall up there. Horicultural Hall was crowded, people would come there to hear Fletcher Henderson play waltzes. He had Louie Armstrong in the band, he had Don Redman , oh, he had a whole -- what's the clarinet player. Buster Bailey. He had all them people and he could arrange and he used to arrange for the…
player, the fellow now, Benny Goodman. Sure.
The man I was talking about, Tom, was named Sam Wooding.
